name: Lament-Gyre
geological_features: Counter-rotating atmospheric bands creating visible shear zones
A descending spiral storm system at the equator
Layers of supercritical fluid between gas and liquid phases
specific_features: Radio emissions that, when processed, produce patterns resembling structured language
description: Lament-Gyre is a gas giant whose most distinctive feature is an equatorial storm system that spirals inward and downward like water circling a drain, a permanent atmospheric feature that pulls cloud material from the upper layers into the crushing depths below. Counter-rotating bands create shear zones visible as dark lines across the planet's surface, dividing its atmosphere into discrete, warring regions.

The planet emits a low, mournful radio frequency that pulses in rhythmic patterns, detected by every vessel that enters the system. In the dense atmosphere, these emissions manifest as infrasonic vibrations that crews report feeling in their chests, a physical sensation of grief that has earned the planet its name.

When the radio emissions are processed through standard linguistic analysis software, they produce patterns that bear a statistical resemblance to structured language, though no meaningful translation has been achieved. The patterns are too complex to be natural atmospheric phenomena and too simple to be definitive communication, trapping analysis in an interpretive limbo that has persisted for decades.

Lament-Gyre's fuel reserves are accessible but unremarkable compared to other gas giants in the region, leaving little practical reason to linger near a world whose primary export is an inexplicable sense of loss. Research stations monitoring the emissions maintain skeleton crews on rotation, as long-term exposure to the infrasonic vibrations produces depression symptoms that resist pharmaceutical intervention.
